responsibilities: Design and deliver scalable analytics and data engineering solutions.
Develop data models, transformation pipelines, and semantic layers.
Translate business requirements into robust, scalable data solutions.
Lead technical workshops and stakeholder discussions.
Drive data quality, testing, documentation, and governance standards.
Identify and proactively manage project risks and blockers.
Mentor colleagues and contribute to the wider data function.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Drive data quality, testing, documentation, and governance standards.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Quality, testing, documentation and governance are given a dedicated responsibility and the summary promises data that is 'trusted', against a single 'fast-paced' mention buried in the desirables.
evidence.domain_risk: An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Senior Analytics Engineer to join a growing organisation that places data at the heart of business decision-making.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: The hiring organisation is never named or sectored and the language is generic business decision-making, with no financial-reporting, regulatory or audit signal.
evidence.collaboration_width: No distinctly named partner teams - only 'technical and non-technical stakeholders' and 'the wider data function'.
evidence.data_team_maturity: Mentor colleagues and contribute to the wider data function.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A data function already exists with colleagues to mentor at a 'growing organisation', but no sub-teams, scale or deployed governance tooling are described.
evidence.jd_authorship: Translate business requirements into robust, scalable data solutions.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Written by a recruitment agency, every bullet is interchangeable boilerplate - no tool, scale figure or methodology appears outside the desirables list.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Develop data models, transformation pipelines, and semantic layers.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: No business function is ever named; the described outputs - data models, transformation frameworks, semantic layers - point at the data function and its consumers.
evidence.autonomy_level: As a Senior Analytics Engineer, you will lead the delivery of analytics and data solutions across a range of business initiatives.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role leads delivery, leads technical workshops, drives quality and governance standards and mentors colleagues - direction-setting rather than scoped delivery.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: AI is never mentioned in the posting, so no AI skill is expected of the candidate.
evidence.testing_framing: Drive data quality, testing, documentation, and governance standards.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing and quality standards are something the candidate drives as a named responsibility, not a tool listed under requirements.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Identify and proactively manage project risks and blockers.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: The only risk named is delivery risk on projects, with quality and governance as one workstream among seven rather than the dominant framing.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Design and deliver scalable analytics and data engineering solutions.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Every infrastructure verb is build-side - design, deliver, develop, build transformation frameworks - with no legacy, migration or remediation language.
evidence.work_arrangement: Fully Remote (UK) | Quarterly Travel to Brighton
evidence.loss_aversion: Drive data quality, testing, documentation, and governance standards - quality is a named workstream but the JD's explicit risk language is about project risks and blockers, not bad data reaching decision-makers. Note: this is a recruitment agency posting; the hiring company is not named, and the stated GBP 90,000 base is a single figure rather than a range so the salary fields are left null.
